description: Maps each DB-stored scenario (by exact title) for the Open Science Transition Uncertainty topic to the 5 curated deck scenarios shown in the Wiley Horizons brief. The DB scenarios are the canonical evidence base; this overlay provides the public-facing framing.

diamond_oa_subscription_erosion.deck_scenario_name: Diamond Open Access & Subscription Model Erosion
diamond_oa_subscription_erosion.primary_signal: Diamond Open Access will become the dominant paradigm, eliminating author fees and democratizing access, while legacy publishers face structural decline.
diamond_oa_subscription_erosion.minority_view: Some legacy publishers may retain niche or high-prestige paywalled offerings, slowing the erosion of subscription models.

decision_fork.favorable: If Diamond Open Access models receive sustained global policy and funding support: subscription models rapidly lose market share; publishers must pivot business models or risk obsolescence.
decision_fork.adverse: If legacy publishers succeed in defending exclusive content or services: hybrid models emerge, with partial preservation of paywalls for high-impact journals.

action_windows.0_6_months: Assess reliance on subscription revenue and exposure to Open Access mandates
action_windows.6_18_months: Develop alternative business models and partnership strategies

recognition_incentives_regional_gaps.deck_scenario_name: Recognition, Incentives & Regional Open Science Gaps
recognition_incentives_regional_gaps.primary_signal: Without reforms to recognition and assessment systems, Open Science adoption will plateau, especially outside top-tier institutions and advanced economies.
recognition_incentives_regional_gaps.minority_view: Some leading research economies may close these gaps faster, setting global best practices and accelerating alignment.

decision_fork.favorable: If new recognition and reward systems are implemented: Open Science practices accelerate, reducing regional disparities and improving research impact.
decision_fork.adverse: If legacy incentive structures persist: Open Science remains a patchwork, with progress stalling in less-incentivized regions.

action_windows.0_6_months: Map incentive structures and identify recognition bottlenecks
action_windows.6_18_months: Pilot alternative assessment and reward frameworks

publishing_integrity_predatory.deck_scenario_name: Publishing Integrity, Predatory Journals & Trust Risks
publishing_integrity_predatory.primary_signal: Predatory and deceptive journals will further undermine confidence in academic publishing, draining resources and distorting research metrics unless systemic countermeasures are adopted.
publishing_integrity_predatory.minority_view: Stronger regulatory interventions or industry self-policing could contain or reverse the proliferation of predatory journals.

decision_fork.favorable: If industry and regulators collaborate on integrity standards: predatory activity is curbed, restoring some trust and funding efficacy.
decision_fork.adverse: If enforcement remains fragmented: predatory journals proliferate, with escalating reputational and financial risks for funders and institutions.

action_windows.0_6_months: Review compliance and legal exposure in cross-border research
action_windows.6_18_months: Engage in policy advocacy or standard-setting consortia

policy_legal_data_sharing_barriers.primary_signal: Fragmented IP, privacy, and national data regulations will impede full-scale Open Science unless coordinated reforms are implemented.
policy_legal_data_sharing_barriers.minority_view: A harmonized international policy framework could resolve many data sharing issues faster than expected.

decision_fork.favorable: If international harmonization and policy reforms progress: open data sharing accelerates, benefiting multi-national research and industry collaboration.
decision_fork.adverse: If legal barriers persist or intensify: data silos remain entrenched; cross-border research and innovation slow.

action_windows.0_6_months: Review compliance and legal exposure in cross-border research
action_windows.6_18_months: Engage in policy advocacy or standard-setting consortia

ai_hybrid_research_ecosystems.deck_scenario_name: AI-Enabled Research Ecosystems & Hybrid Open-Closed Models
ai_hybrid_research_ecosystems.primary_signal: Automated, AI-powered research, global infrastructures, and hybrid models will define a new equilibrium - balancing openness for collaboration with proprietary controls for commercial and security reasons.
ai_hybrid_research_ecosystems.minority_view: Concerns over security, privacy, and IP may prompt a reversion to more closed, proprietary approaches in select sectors.

decision_fork.favorable: If AI platforms and infrastructures integrate robust privacy/security controls: hybrid models dominate, enabling safe public-private research and accelerating global knowledge sharing.
decision_fork.adverse: If security and sovereignty risks escalate: balkanized research ecosystems emerge, with fragmented standards and reduced international collaboration.

action_windows.0_6_months: Identify readiness for AI-enabled research and hybrid model adoption
action_windows.6_18_months: Invest in platform integration and security upgrades
